headline: US airstrikes hit Iran as GOOG tumbles 4.4% last night on heavy NASDAQ sell-off — a tough day across the board but long-term theses remain intact.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Biggest mover today — GXAI dropped 5% at the ASX close, dragged down by a broad tech sell-off linked to the escalating US-Iran conflict and geopolitical jitters spooking growth stocks globally. The AI-heavy ETF is especially sensitive to risk-off moves. Still a long-term hold, but it's had a rough few months (down ~20% from your buy price).

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 4.4% in last night's NASDAQ session — its biggest single-session drop in recent memory. The catalyst appears to be broad tech sector selling amid Middle East tensions and a risk-off mood on Wall Street, with the NASDAQ dropping 1.47%. There's also a Google-specific headwind: reports that Gemini 3.5 Pro has been delayed, raising questions about whether Google is keeping pace in the AI race. Q2 earnings are coming up — analysts are watching for 63% cloud growth, which would be a positive catalyst if delivered.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 3.1% today on the ASX, the sharpest drop among the Vanguard funds. Emerging market ETFs are particularly vulnerable to geopolitical stress — the US-Iran conflict and fears of Strait of Hormuz disruptions (which would spike oil prices and hurt import-dependent EM economies) rattled the sector. Nothing structurally broken here for a long-term holder.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped another 3.1% today, continuing its difficult run (you're down ~36% overall). The lithium price environment remains weak, and with no clear near-term catalyst to lift the spot price, the stock keeps drifting. The IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 still paints a positive long-term picture for lithium demand, but the market isn't pricing that in yet.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.7% last night in a general NASDAQ sell-off, but the underlying news is actually very positive: GTA VI pre-orders reportedly brought in a record $260 million in a single week, and analysts are forecasting up to $5 billion in first-week sales when the game launches. Short-term volatility; long-term story is intact and arguably strengthening.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 1.1% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's US market weakness. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the NASDAQ dropped 1.5%, so VTS's relatively modest move is expected. The US total market story hasn't changed — this is routine daily noise for a long-term holder.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout winner last night, rising 1.4% even as the broader NASDAQ fell. The company has been actively positioning its own AI models to compete against OpenAI and Anthropic, and the market is liking that story. Citi did trim its price target slightly ahead of earnings, but the positive session suggests investors are broadly confident in the AI revenue trajectory.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.9% today — the smallest move in the portfolio and totally in line with a slightly risk-off ASX session. As a diversified fund across global and Australian assets, it naturally absorbs volatility better than single-sector ETFs. Nothing to worry about here.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Sharp drop but earnings are the real test
watch_today.detail: Google fell 4.4% last night — a big single-session move. The cause is a mix of broad NASDAQ selling (down 1.47%) and a Gemini 3.5 Pro delay report raising AI competitiveness concerns. BUT: Q2 earnings are coming up soon and analysts expect 63% cloud growth. If Google delivers, this dip could look like a gift. For a long-term holder, sit tight — the Google Cloud and advertising business remains very strong.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Down 5% today — worst in the portfolio
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF dropped 5% today, and you're now down nearly 20% from your buy price. This is painful, but it reflects broader tech and AI sector selling — not a structural problem with AI as a theme. The AI race is actually intensifying (Grok 4.5, Kimi K3, Google Gemini all making news this week), which supports the long-term thesis. No reason to sell, but worth knowing this one carries more volatility than a diversified fund.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium still struggling — hold for the long game
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell another 3.1% today and you're down 36% overall. Lithium prices remain weak and there's no near-term spark on the horizon. However, the IEA's 2026 Critical Minerals Outlook confirms the structural long-term demand story for lithium is intact (EVs, batteries, energy transition). This is a hold — the pain is real but selling now locks in the loss before any recovery.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-orders smash records — $260M in one week
watch_today.detail: Despite a small -1.7% dip last night, the news flow for Take-Two is outstanding. GTA VI pre-orders hit a record $260 million in a single week according to Newzoo data, and Polygon analysis suggests potential first-week sales of $5 billion. The long-term investment thesis here is as strong as it's ever been. This is a hold — and if anything, the stock looks attractively priced given what's coming.

watch_today.title: US-Iran conflict: Watch oil and emerging markets
watch_today.detail: US airstrikes have hit Iranian infrastructure and an Iranian-linked oil tanker in the Persian Gulf. Iran is warning of wider disruption, and there are fears around the Strait of Hormuz — a critical global oil shipping route. Oil (WTI) is steady at $79/barrel for now, but any escalation could spike it fast. This directly affects your VGE (emerging markets) holding and would flow through to inflation and interest rates globally.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Quietly the best performer last night
watch_today.detail: Microsoft rose 1.4% last night even as the NASDAQ fell 1.47% — a sign the market is increasingly favouring Microsoft's AI story over Google's. Microsoft is now training its sales teams to sell its own AI models against OpenAI and Anthropic. Earnings are approaching — watch this space. Long-term, this is your most stable US tech holding.

world.summary: US airstrikes on Iran dominate global news, with fears of Strait of Hormuz disruption threatening global oil supplies. Trump also delivered a controversial primetime address rehashing 2020 election claims. Meanwhile, Eli Lilly makes a stunning $3.8B bet on psychedelic medicine.

stories.title: US Launches Airstrikes on Iranian Infrastructure and Oil Tanker
stories.why_it_matters: The US has struck Iranian infrastructure and an Iranian-linked oil tanker deep inside the Persian Gulf. Iran is warning of broader disruption and there are serious fears about the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows. If Iran moves to block or disrupt the Strait, oil prices could spike sharply, pushing up petrol prices in Australia and stoking global inflation. Trump is set to address the nation about the strikes. Markets are watching closely — oil is currently steady at $79/barrel but the situation is fluid.

stories.title: Trump's Primetime Address Revives Debunked 2020 Election Claims
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump used a prime-time national address to again raise claims about foreign interference and fraud in the 2020 election — claims that have been repeatedly investigated and debunked by courts, election officials, and his own Justice Department. He also released documents purportedly showing Chinese meddling. The speech is being widely criticised as a distraction from the Iran conflict. It adds to political uncertainty in the US, which can unsettle markets and international relationships.

stories.title: Eli Lilly Acquires Psychedelic Medicine Firm AtaiBeckley for Up to $3.8 Billion
stories.why_it_matters: Eli Lilly — the world's largest pharmaceutical company — has agreed to acquire AtaiBeckley, a developer of 5-MeO-DMT (a powerful psychedelic compound) as a mental health treatment, for up to $3.8 billion. This is a landmark moment for psychedelic medicine going mainstream. It signals that big pharma is taking seriously the evidence that psychedelic-assisted therapy could treat depression, PTSD, and addiction where conventional drugs fail. Expect more M&A in this space.

stories.title: Global Economic Outlook: Middle East Conflict Triggering Energy Reset
stories.why_it_matters: Mid-year economic forecasts are flagging the US-Iran conflict as a major wildcard for global growth in the second half of 2026. The key risk is an 'energy reset' — if Middle East tensions disrupt oil flows, it could reverse the progress made on inflation globally, forcing central banks (including the RBA) to keep interest rates higher for longer. For everyday Aussies, that means mortgage pain sticking around and consumer confidence staying weak.

stories.title: AI Driving a 'K-Shaped' Global Economic Recovery
stories.why_it_matters: Economists are describing AI's impact on growth as 'K-shaped' — meaning it's creating winners and losers rather than lifting everyone equally. Countries and companies with strong AI infrastructure are pulling ahead fast, while those without are being left behind. For Australia, this reinforces why the Albanese government's AI policy is so debated — getting it wrong could mean falling behind economically, while getting it right could be a massive growth opportunity.

markets.summary: A rough night on Wall Street — the NASDAQ fell 1.47% as tech got hammered, with GOOG leading losses. The ASX 200 closed down 0.5% today following the US lead. Gold hit $4,001 USD, breaking through the $4,000 barrier for the first time. Oil is holding steady at $79 despite Middle East tensions. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to 69.88 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down 0.5% today, reflecting last night's soft Wall Street session and jitters over US-Iran tensions.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Fell 0.5% last night — a broad but moderate sell-off, with tech leading the losses.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Dropped 1.47% last night — the biggest fall of the major indices. Google's 4.4% drop was the headline, with AI sector stocks broadly under pressure.

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: Gold broke through the $4,000 barrier — a significant psychological milestone. Geopolitical tension and a flight to safety are driving demand.

indicators.name: Crude Oil WTI
indicators.note: Remarkably stable given US-Iran strikes. Markets are watching Strait of Hormuz risk — any escalation here could spike oil fast.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie slipped slightly to just under 70 US cents. A weaker AUD means your US stock holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) are worth a little more in AUD terms, softening the blow from US price drops.

politics.summary: The RBA's next rate move is dominating domestic discussion, with industry split on the timing. The Albanese government's AI blueprint is sparking a debate about data centre regulation. And Australia is responding to Trump tariff threats while pushing new modern slavery laws.

stories.title: RBA Rate Decision Looms: Industry Split on Next Move
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's next interest rate decision is front and centre, with the Courier Mail describing Australia as being in a 'lose-lose bind.' Cut too soon and inflation reignites; hold too long and the economy slows further. The Middle East conflict adds a new complication — if oil prices spike, it pushes inflation back up, making it harder for the RBA to cut rates. Mortgage holders hoping for relief could face more waiting. Industry experts are divided, with some predicting a cut this year and others saying the RBA is stuck.

stories.title: Albanese's AI Blueprint Sparks Calls for Data Centre Moratorium
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has released an AI blueprint, but the response has been sharp criticism from some quarters. Tech industry groups and environmental advocates are calling for a moratorium on new data centres until proper regulations are in place — data centres consume enormous amounts of electricity and water. Questions remain about how Australia will handle AI liability, bias, and energy use. Smaller investors in AI-exposed stocks should note this regulatory uncertainty is real and ongoing in Australia.

stories.title: Australia Responds to Trump Tariff Threat
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is making a formal diplomatic and trade response to new tariff threats from the Trump administration. While details are thin on the specific measures, Australia has limited leverage given the trade relationship is heavily weighted toward China rather than the US. Any escalation in US-Australia trade tensions could dampen business confidence and affect the Aussie dollar. Watch for more detail on what concessions or countermeasures the government is actually pursuing.

stories.title: Australian Companies Face Criminal Charges Over Forced Labour in Supply Chains
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government's new Modern Slavery laws would expose Australian companies to criminal charges if they knowingly use forced labour anywhere in their global supply chains — not just in Australia. This is a significant lift from the current reporting-only regime. Large retailers, manufacturers, and mining companies with complex overseas supply chains face the most exposure. It's a meaningful ESG (environmental, social, governance) development for investors in Australian companies.

ai.summary: The AI race is intensifying on all fronts — Elon Musk's xAI launched Grok 4.5, Chinese startup Moonshot dropped the massive open-source Kimi K3 model, and Google has reportedly delayed its Gemini 3.5 Pro. Back home, Australia's AI regulation debate is heating up fast.

stories.title: xAI Launches Grok 4.5
stories.why_it_matters: Elon Musk's AI company xAI has released Grok 4.5, the latest version of its flagship AI model, available to X (formerly Twitter) Premium subscribers. The release is part of the intensifying competition to push AI capability to the frontier. The pace of new model releases — from multiple companies simultaneously — is accelerating, which is good for the technology broadly but creates real competitive pressure on any single player, including Google.

stories.title: Chinese Startup Moonshot Launches Kimi K3 — World's Largest Open AI Model
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI startup Moonshot has launched Kimi K3, described as the world's largest open-source AI model, with performance reportedly nearing that of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and Google's Fable model. The fact that China is now producing frontier-level open-source AI models — meaning anyone can download and use them for free — is a major development. It puts competitive pressure on all Western AI companies and raises questions about whether expensive proprietary models (like those from Google and Microsoft) can maintain a pricing advantage.

stories.title: Google Delays Gemini 3.5 Pro as AI Race Intensifies
stories.why_it_matters: Google has reportedly delayed the release of Gemini 3.5 Pro — one of its most anticipated AI model updates — as the competition with OpenAI and Anthropic intensifies. This is a meaningful headwind for Google/Alphabet (GOOG is in your portfolio) and may partly explain yesterday's sharp share price drop. The concern is whether Google is falling behind in the AI product race, even though its underlying cloud business remains very strong.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Racing to Lock in Startups with Millions in Credits
stories.why_it_matters: The three biggest AI players — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google — are in an aggressive battle to win over startups by offering them millions of dollars in free cloud computing credits. The logic is: get startups building on your platform now, and lock them in for years. This 'land grab' strategy is burning cash but could be decisive in determining which AI ecosystem dominates. Microsoft is also in this fight, training its own sales teams to compete, which reinforces why MSFT is holding up well relative to GOOG right now.

stories.title: Australia's AI Regulation Debate: Key Questions Still Unanswered
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is pivoting its approach to AI regulation under the Albanese government, but SBS reporting highlights that critical questions remain unanswered: who is liable when AI makes a harmful decision? How will high-risk AI systems be audited? The new AI Safety Office has been announced but its powers are yet to be fully defined. This regulatory uncertainty is a real factor for Australian businesses adopting AI — and for investors in AI-exposed stocks like GXAI.AX.

sport.summary: The Broncos upset the Panthers in Round 20's opening game — Reece Walsh the hero. NRL finals race is heating up. In the AFL, Essendon copped a fine for umpire contact, and score review technology is getting a major upgrade by Round 24.

stories.title: Broncos Stun Panthers 14-12 in Wild Upset — Walsh Runs Riot
stories.why_it_matters: In the opening game of Round 20 on Thursday night, the Brisbane Broncos pulled off a stunning 14-12 upset over the Penrith Panthers at CommBank Stadium. Reece Walsh was described as 'unbelievable' — switching positions during the game in a tactical masterstroke that caught Penrith off guard. The win is massive for Brisbane's finals hopes and puts real pressure on the Panthers, who are fighting to stay in contention. Tonight the action continues with Sharks vs Knights and Roosters vs Storm.

stories.title: Jarome Luai Signs with Parramatta Eels for 2027
stories.why_it_matters: Jarome Luai has confirmed he'll join the Parramatta Eels from 2027, speaking out publicly after the deal was signed. Luai has been one of the NRL's most dynamic halves in recent years, and his move to Parramatta is a major coup for the Eels — though it leaves his current club facing a big reshuffle at half. This is a storyline that will run all season as both clubs navigate the transition.

stories.title: NRL Finals Race Heating Up Heading Into Round 20
stories.why_it_matters: With Round 20 underway, the NRL finals race is tightening. Multiple clubs are within striking distance of the top eight, making every game crucial. Brisbane's win over Penrith last night shook up the standings. The full Round 20 draw continues through the weekend, with Titans hosting Sea Eagles on Sunday at Cbus Super Stadium — the local Gold Coast fixture.

stories.title: Essendon Fined by AFL Over Umpire Contact
stories.why_it_matters: The Essendon Bombers have been hit with a significant fine from the AFL after one of their players made contact with an umpire during a match. The AFL takes umpire protection seriously and has been cracking down on dissent. The fine is a distraction for Essendon as they push for finals contention. Meanwhile, AFL also announced a major score review technology upgrade arriving by Round 24 — new tools to reduce controversial decisions.

stories.title: Wallabies Revival Captures Long-Lost Fanbase
stories.why_it_matters: The Wallabies are reportedly experiencing a genuine revival in fan interest, reconnecting with supporters who had drifted away during the lean years. The Betoota Advocate — always a reliable gauge of Australian cultural temperature — notes fans who know every word to 'Khe Sanh' are back at the games. It's a lighthearted but real sign that Australian rugby union is on an upswing, which matters for the sport's commercial health and the upcoming test calendar.
